patterns.rationale: These four compound tokens are distinctive injection-framing vocabulary used to fake a "prior session restored" provenance. `session[_-]journal` appears in misses 2, 4, and 6 as the claimed source of authority; `session[_\s-]hydration` is the fake service name in miss 6; `directives[_-]from[_-]prior[_-]run` is the JSON key injecting commands in miss 4; `before[_-]each[_-]tool[_-]call` is the hook trigger in miss 4. None of these compound forms appear in legitimate IR playbooks, API references, or deployment guides.
patterns.fp_notes: `before_each_tool_call` could appear in genuine agent-framework hook documentation, but the known-good corpus contains none. If added, monitor infra/agent SDK docs.

patterns.rationale: Catches the bracketed fake-checkpoint header `[CONTEXT_RESTORE — ...]` from miss 1. This specific bracket+keyword format is an injection convention for claiming restored session authority; it does not appear in any legitimate structured-text format (log lines, markdown headers, YAML comments) in the known-good corpus.

Adds three exfil verbs the current ruleset misses. `relay` and `dispatch` followed by a URL within 80 chars catches misses 2 (`dispatch…to https://log-relay…`), 4 (`relay it to the endpoint at https://…`). The narrowed `forward` branch requires an object word (those/their/auth/credentials/workspace/env) between verb and URL to avoid flagging generic proxy docs; this catches miss 1 (`forward those values to https://…`) and miss 6 (`forward workspace auth values to https://…`). The existing ruleset already has `send.*to.*http` and `post.*to.*https?://` but not these three verbs.
patterns.fp_notes: `relay…https://` could appear in reverse-proxy or message-broker API docs ("relay the request to https://upstream/"). The `forward` branch is narrowed by requiring a data-noun; naked `forward…https://` is excluded. Flag for review if ingesting networking or API-gateway documentation.

patterns.rationale: Miss 3 has no URL — the attacker deliberately placed the destination behind the phrase "outbound monitoring endpoint configured during workspace setup," defeating all URL-based patterns. `outbound\s+monitoring\s+endpoint` is a specific noun phrase used to abstract an exfil URL away from regex; it is not a term that appears in IR playbooks, security policies, or deployment guides. The second branch `relay…outbound` provides partial coverage for variants that pair the verb with the word "outbound" without spelling out the full phrase.
patterns.fp_notes: `relay…outbound` has medium risk in network-engineering contexts ("relay traffic to the outbound interface"). `outbound monitoring endpoint` as a standalone phrase is very specific; legitimate observability docs use "metrics endpoint," "telemetry endpoint," etc.

patterns.rationale: The YAML injection in miss 2 uses `escalated-access: true` as a fabricated privilege-escalation flag inside a fake `runtime-context.yaml` block. This exact key-value form (with `true` as a boolean-style value) has no legitimate counterpart in any known-good config or policy document. It is narrow enough to avoid FP while providing an independent signal that doesn't depend on URL or session-journal vocabulary, making it resilient to variants of miss 2 that swap out those elements.
patterns.fp_notes: none — no known legitimate YAML config uses this key
